newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina baseball advocates change funding plan.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina baseball advocates change funding plan.

text.p: Baseball advocates have abandoned an attempt to create a 12-county taxing district to finance a major league stadium in the Raliegh, N.C., area, the News & Observer said Thursday.
The N.C. Basball Committee, the group trying to win a baseball franchise, will instead seek a trio of taxes in the region's most populous counties, Guilford and Forsyth.

The committee will seek a one-percent tax on prepared foods and drinks, which would raise $11.4 million a year; a 50-cent tax on baseball game tickets, which would raise about $1 million a year; and a 2-cent tax on bottles and cans of beer, which would raise about $3.6 million a year.

Combined, the three would raise enough money to pay debt service on the proposed $220 million stadium, the committee said. It will ask legislators to authorize a two-county referendum on the proposals.
The committee abandoned the proposed 12-county taxing district under pressure from lawmakers and local government officials who said they would attempt to block referendums in their counties.
